2021 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxiliary) City Civil & Sessions Court,
Court No.28, Ahmedabad in M.A.C.P. No.285/2011 whereby the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the claim petition and awarded as sum of Rs. 6,74,800 as NEUTRAL CITATION United India Insurance Company Ltd vs Babubhai Punaji Ganchi on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8785611/

sentences.text:
The facts leading to the filing of the captioned appeal, as narrated in the claim petition and as emerging from the record of the Tribunal, are that on 14.05.2009, Dariaben alias Diwaben Babubhai Ghanchini, (hereinafter called as deceased), she was traveling in motor car bearing registration No.
MH-1-U-3481 along with family members and when she reached at the place of the accident, the said car dashed with the trailer herein bearing registration No. HR-47-A-6741 from the behind.
It has been further submitted that the said trailer was parked on the road in breach of traffic rules without any indicator or signal.
3. Due to the impact of the incident, the said Dariaben alias Diwaben Babubhai Ghanchini succumbed to the injuries.

It has been further averred that at the time of accident, the deceased NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1704/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined was aged about 21 year and she was earning Rs.10,000/- per annum, therefore, the claim petition for seeking the compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- came to be filed.

4. Having been served with the notices of the claim petition, the Opponent No.1, 2 and 4 before the learned Tribunal have chosen not to appear, however, the Appellant- Respondent No.3 filed the written statement vide Exhibit-39 thereby denying the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for rejection, while Opponent No.5 before the learned Tribunal filed the written statement,
thereby denying the contentions raised in the claim petition and prayed for rejection.
5.
Having considered the pleadings of the parties, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues at Exhibit-42:

1. Have the applicant(s) proved that the deceased died due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1704/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined of the offending vehicle involved in the accident?"
2.
Whether the Applicant/s are entitled to compensation?
If yes, what amount, from whom, and at what rate of interest?
3.What order and award?

6. Having consider the pleadings, evidence adduced by the parties and submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the respective parties, the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the claim petition.

7. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award, the Appellant-Insurance Company of the offending car bearing registration No. MH-1-U-3481 preferred the captioned appeal thereby, challenging the impugned judgment and award.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties Ms. Kirti Pathak, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Appellant- NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1704/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined Insurance Company,
vehemently submitted that the policy, which came to be issued by the Appellant is an act only policy, therefore, the risk of the Occupant in the car is not covered in the policy.
She further submitted that at the time of the accident, the decease was traveling in the car as Occupant.

She further submitted that having regard to the terms and condition of the policy, the learned Tribunal ought to have exonerated the Insurance Company from satisfying the award, however, the learned Tribunal has saddled the liability on Respondent No.3 to satisfy the award.
She further submitted that the impugned judgment and award is not sustainable, therefore, the same is liable to be modified.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant(s) supported the impugned judgment and submitted that there are no infirmities in it; therefore, the captioned matter is liable to be dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1704/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined 10.

Having considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and having gone through the record, it is to be noted that, at the time of the accident, the deceased Dariaben alias Diwaben Babubhai Ghanchini was traveling in the car.
It has been argued on behalf of the Appellant-Insurance Company that the risk of the decease was not covered under the policy.
The policy has been proved at Exhibit-67.

Perusal of the policy transpires that the Insurance Company has charged the premium as shown as under:-
1. B: T.P-BASIC- 2500/-

2 . For Third Party Property Damage of 6000 IMT-20 -100/-
3. Compulsory PA to Owner-Driver Amount-200,000/- 100/-
stamp duty 1/-

Total Liability Premium Rs. 2,500/-
11.
It is settled preposition of law that the insurer is first party while the Insurance Company is called the second party and all other persons are called third party.
Being a third NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1704/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined party, the risk of Dariaben alias Diwaben Babubhai Ghanchini was covered under the policy.

The learned Tribunal after considering the ratio of the judgment rendered by Gujarat High Court in case of Hamendrasinh Mansingh Jadav v.
Sanjaybhai Govindbhai Dabhi, 2018 C.J. (Gujarat) 813, observed that the Dariaben alias Diwaben Babubhai Ghanchini being the third party, hence the risk is covered United India Insurance Company Ltd vs Babubhai Punaji Ganchi on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8785611/
3 under the policy.

Hamendrasinh Mansingh Jadav v.
Sanjaybhai Govindbhai Dabhi, 2018 C.J. (Gujarat) 813
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd vs Babubhai Punaji Ganchi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In case of Hamendrasinh Mansingh Jadav (supra), the Gujarat High Court observed as under:-
"The Court took the view that the Occupant or the passenger in private car is/are included withing the expression of third party, therefore, the risk of the Occupant is covered whether the only policy or other policy and Insurance Company is liable to indemnify."
12.
The learned Tribunal further observed that the said judgment was challenged by the Insurance Company by way of preferring the Special Leave Petition (c) No.3762 of 2019, which came to be dismissed.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Gujarat High Court in case of Hamendrasinh Mansingh NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1704/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 02/04/2026 undefined Jadav v. Sanjaybhai Govindbhai Dabhi, 2018 C.J. (Gujarat) 813, in my considered view, the learned Tribunal has not committed any error in holding that the Appellant Insurance Company is liable to satisfy the award passed by the learned Tribunal.

sentences.text: 13. Thus, in view of the above discussion, there is no infirmity in the impugned judgment and award as the same is just and proper.
14. In view of the above discussion, the captioned appeal stands dismissed.
No order as to costs.
The Record and Proceedings (R&P) shall be sent back to the concerned court/Tribunal forthwith.

Statutory amount, if any, lying deposited with the Registry of the Court be transmitted to the concerned learned Tribunal forthwith.
